question: Which of the following playback singers is the recipient of the Karnataka Ratna Award 2005?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimsen Joshi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi** was a renowned Indian vocalist in the Hindustani classical tradition.
 
• He was awarded the **Karnataka Ratna** in 2005, which is the highest civilian honor of the state of Karnataka.
 
• Bhimsen Joshi was also the recipient of other prestigious awards such as the Bharat Ratna in 2008 and Padma Vibhushan in 1999.
 
• His contribution to Hindustani classical music and his exceptional vocal renditions have made him a celebrated figure in Indian music history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karnataka Ratna Award**

 
 
• The Karnataka Ratna is the highest civilian award in the state of Karnataka, India.
 
• It was instituted in the year 1992 by the Government of Karnataka.
 
• The award is presented in recognition of extraordinary contributions to the state in various fields such as literature, culture, education, politics, science, and public service.
 
• Some other notable recipients of the Karnataka Ratna include Kuvempu, Dr. Rajkumar, and Sri Sri Shivakumara Swamiji.
 
 
 
• **Bhimsen Joshi**
 
 
• Bhimsen Joshi was born on February 4, 1922, in Gadag, Karnataka.
 
• He was a prominent exponent of the Khayal form of singing and belonged to the Kirana Gharana.
 
• His music career spanned over seven decades, and he was known for his powerful voice and unique style.
 
• In addition to classical music, Bhimsen Joshi also performed devotional music and popularized classical music among the masses.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music**
 
 
• It is one of the two main forms of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• Hindustani classical music has a rich history and has been passed down through generations by oral tradition.
 
• The main forms of Hindustani music include Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri, and Tappa.
 
• It emphasizes improvisation and exploration of all aspects of a raga.
